# San Angelo writes data centers into its zoning code and makes them a conditional use only

San Angelo created Section 430 of its zoning ordinance, the first full land use rulebook for data centers in West Texas. New data centers are allowed as a principal use only by Conditional Use, and only in Light Manufacturing and Heavy Manufacturing districts. Each one comes back to a public hearing. The code caps buildings at 75 feet. It bars ground mounted equipment near residentially zoned property and limits noise to 55 dBa at the property line day and night. It also requires a sound modeling study before final site plan approval and a post development sound study after occupancy. The definition it adopted excludes cryptocurrency mining. The ordinance was introduced on May 5th, 2026 and passed on May 19th, 2026.

- Topic: data-centers
- Decided by: City of San Angelo City Council (city)
- Where: Tom Green
- Statistical areas:
  - San Angelo, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Public meeting
- Take part: https://www.sanangelo.gov/803/Data-Center-Information

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2026-04-20 · hearing: Planning Commission public hearing and recommendation for approval
- 2026-04-22 · hearing: City Council special meeting for public input on the data center project and regulations
- 2026-05-05 · hearing: Introduced with public hearing
- 2026-05-19 · ordered: Finally passed by City Council, reported 6 to 0
- 2026-05-19 · effective: Ordinance effective date

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-19 · Checked and unchanged. The land use regulations approved May 19th are still the governing action listed, and the city's page carries nothing from July or August.
- 2026-08-22 · Checked and unchanged. The zoning ordinance still amends Chapter 12 on planning and development to create a specific use standard for data centers, and the city's record carries no later amendment to it.
- 2026-08-26 · Checked and unchanged. Data centers are still written into the zoning code as a conditional use and the ordinance text is unchanged.
- 2026-08-29 · Checked and unchanged. Data centers are still a defined use in the zoning code and still a conditional use rather than a permitted one. The council has not amended the definition since adopting it.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### New data centers are permitted only by Conditional Use and only in the two manufacturing districts.

> New data centers shall be permitted as a principal use by Conditional Use (CU) only, in accordance with procedures set forth in Section 208.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### Conditional Use applications may be made only within Light Manufacturing and Heavy Manufacturing districts.

> An application for a CU may be made within ML (Light Manufacturing) and MH (Heavy Manufacturing) Districts.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### Building height is capped at 75 feet.

> Maximum Height: 75 feet, measured at the top of the building plate (roof deck).

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### Noise is limited to 55 dBa at the property line during the day and at night.

> Any noise that emanates from all activity associated with any data center is  limited to a maximum sound level of 55 dBa during the daytime and 55 dBa at  nighttime.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### The adopted definition of a data center excludes cryptocurrency mining.

> A data center  shall not include cryptocurrency mining.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### The ordinance was introduced on May 5th, 2026 and passed on May 19th, 2026.

> INTRODUCED with public hearing the 5th day of May 2026, and finally PASSED this 19th day of  May, 2026.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2255

### The City of San Angelo reports the land use regulations passed 6 to 0.

> Approved 6-0 at the May 19, 2026 City Council meeting.

Source (primary_official): https://www.sanangelo.gov/803/Data-Center-Information

# San Angelo sets reporting rules for data center coolant discharged into the city sewer

San Angelo adopted Ordinance 2026-076, which adds a data center subsection to the city's prohibited discharges rule. Any intentional release of treated cooling fluid into the sanitary sewer is defined as a discharge event, and sampling with laboratory verification has to be completed before each one. Records of volumes, results and dates must be kept for at least three years and handed to the Director of Water Utilities on request. Planned discharges need 72 hours written notice. Emergency discharges have to be reported within 4 hours with a written incident report inside 7 days. The council introduced the ordinance on May 19th, 2026 and adopted it on June 2nd, 2026.

- Topic: land-water-and-permitting
- Decided by: City of San Angelo City Council (city)
- Where: Tom Green
- Statistical areas:
  - San Angelo, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Public meeting

# Reeves County Emergency Services District No. 2 takes up a Chapter 312 abatement for a gas plant built to run data centers

A small emergency services district in Pecos noticed a public hearing to accept a tax abatement application from Energy Forge One LLC under Chapter 312 of the Texas Tax Code. The application concerns a new gas turbine power generation facility inside the Energy Forge One Reinvestment Zone. That zone was established on November 24th, 2025. The notice describes the plant as producing dedicated power for prospective data center end users. It puts the estimated project cost at $6 billion. The hearing was set for 5.30 in the afternoon on March 25th, 2026 at the district's administrative office in Pecos. All interested persons were free to appear and present testimony. The outcome of that hearing has not been confirmed from district minutes.

# Pecos-Barstow-Toyah ISD's JETI agreement for the Energy Forge One power plant is executed and posted

The Texas Comptroller now lists application J0022 among current agreements under the Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation Act. It pairs Energy Forge One LLC with Pecos-Barstow-Toyah ISD in Reeves County. The executed agreement was posted on July 24th, 2026. The recommendation packet had gone up on February 11th, 2026. JETI excludes data centers from eligibility. This project entered the program as fossil fuel electric power generation, which is why it also carries no minimum job requirement. The Comptroller's table records a proposed investment of $6.5 billion. Reporting by Grist says the school board approved the application at a February meeting and puts the value of the break at more than $227 million over ten years.

- Topic: state-policy
- Decided by: Pecos-Barstow-Toyah Independent School District Board of Trustees (school-district)
- Where: Reeves
- Statistical areas:
  - Town of Pecos, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Write to the decider
- Take part: https://comptroller.texas.gov/economy/development/prop-tax/jeti/application-details.php?id=J0022

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2025-11-10 · filed: Application posted by the Comptroller
- 2026-02-11 · ordered: Comptroller recommendation packet posted
- 2026-07-24 · signed: Executed agreement posted by the Comptroller
- 2026-07-24 · filed: Agreement document posted to the state's application record

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-19 · The agreement itself is now posted. The state's application record for the Energy Forge One project added an agreement document dated July 24th, and the application has still not been executed.
- 2026-08-22 · Checked and unchanged. The state's application record for the Energy Forge One project still carries the agreement document dated July 24th, and the application is still not executed.
- 2026-08-26 · Checked and unchanged. The agreement still stands. The comptroller's own current agreements table still carries Energy Forge One under the Pecos-Barstow-Toyah school district, which is the state's own confirmation that it is live.
- 2026-08-29 · Checked and unchanged. The school district's agreement for the Energy Forge One plant still stands, and the state rather than the district still carries the cost of the abatement. Nothing on the Comptroller's record alters the agreement.

# Tom Green County Commissioners Court declines a Precinct 4 moratorium on data centers and large energy projects

The Tom Green County Commissioners Court voted not to pursue a temporary moratorium on large scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4. The court acted after hearing a presentation from Beacon Data Centers on its proposed Westline site at Dove Creek, west of San Angelo. Commissioner Shawn Nanny pointed to a $100 million lawsuit filed against Hill County after that county approved a similar one year pause. The result is that the unincorporated part of the county has no local pause. The city of San Angelo has three adopted data center ordinances, and they apply only inside its own limits. That split is the whole local story in Texas, where counties have no general zoning power and cities do.

- Topic: data-centers
- Decided by: Tom Green County Commissioners Court (county)
- Where: Tom Green
- Statistical areas:
  - San Angelo, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Public meeting
- Take part: https://sanangelolive.com/news/county/2026-06-02/tom-green-county-commissioners-reject-data-center-moratorium

- Last checked: 2026-08-28

## Dates

- 2026-06-02 · ordered: Commissioners Court declined to advance the Precinct 4 moratorium

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-19 · Checked and unchanged. The court still declines to pursue a temporary moratorium on large scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4. The reasoning given remains the limits of county authority and the risk of litigation.
- 2026-08-22 · Checked and unchanged. The court still declines to pursue a temporary moratorium on large scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4. The reasoning given is still the limits of county authority.
- 2026-08-25 · Checked and unchanged. The decision still stands as decided.
- 2026-08-28 · Checked and unchanged. Tom Green County still has no moratorium in Precinct 4, so the Westline site at Dove Creek is still subject only to the rules a county already holds.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The court voted against a temporary moratorium on large scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4 after a Beacon Data Centers presentation.

> SAN ANGELO, Texas — The Tom Green County Commissioners' Court voted Tuesday not to pursue a temporary moratorium on large-scale energy and data center development in Precinct 4 after hearing a presentation from Beacon Data Centers about its proposed Westline Site in Dove Creek.

Source (journalism): https://sanangelolive.com/news/county/2026-06-02/tom-green-county-commissioners-reject-data-center-moratorium

### A commissioner cited litigation against Hill County over a similar moratorium.

> Commissioner Shawn Nanny referenced a recent $100 million lawsuit filed against Hill County after it approved a similar one-year moratorium.

Source (journalism): https://sanangelolive.com/news/county/2026-06-02/tom-green-county-commissioners-reject-data-center-moratorium

# SpaceX will build the Terafab semiconductor plant in Grimes County on a state grant and two school district agreements

Governor Greg Abbott announced on August 6th, 2026 that SpaceX will construct a vertically integrated semiconductor fabrication plant in Grimes County. A Texas Enterprise Fund grant of $30 million has been extended to the company. The project is also qualified under the state's Jobs Energy Technology and Innovation program. The release states a first phase of more than $16.8 billion in capital investment and 3,000 new jobs. The company's own statement in the release says the plant will produce AI chips at scale. Two school districts have agreements of their own. The Iola board voted to enter one and the Anderson-Shiro superintendent describes another.

# Governor Abbott directs the utility commission and ERCOT to audit every data center in the interconnection queue before any advances

Governor Greg Abbott issued a directive on August 3rd, 2026. It tells the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to run a verification and audit of every data center moving through the interconnection process. The audit must finish before any data center project moves forward. The directive names five things the agencies must obtain from each project. They are public financial assistance received or expected. They are whether the project brings its own power and whether it brings and reuses its own water. They are what it does to reduce effects on neighbors and who owns and controls it. The letter states the queue at approximately 474 gigawatts and puts the data center share of new power requests at approximately 90 percent. It gives a reason. Some data centers did not answer the commission's own survey of water and power use.

- Topic: data-centers
- Decided by: Office of the Texas Governor (governor)
- Where: Statewide
- Status: pending
- Public access: Public meeting
- Take part: https://gov.texas.gov/uploads/files/press/Thomas_Gleeson_Pablo_Vegas_Data_Centers_Directive_Letter_to_PUCT_ERCOT_August_2026_.pdf

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2026-08-03 · ordered: Directive issued
- 2026-08-07 · statutory deadline: Batch Zero classification deadline set in the ERCOT Planning Guide passed with no classification notified
- 2026-08-20 · hearing: Utility commission open meeting carrying ERCOT's request for a good cause exception, agenda item 22
- 2026-08-20 · ordered: Commission order granting the good cause exceptions, filed in Project No. 59142
- 2026-08-31 · statutory deadline: Date the grid operator asked to conditionally classify large loads by, in place of the August 7th deadline
- 2026-12-10 · statutory deadline: Both the eligibility verification report and the community impact review report are to be filed
- 2026-12-17 · hearing: Commission open meeting that takes up the two reports

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-16 · The directive letter itself is now the cited source rather than the press release about it. The release reads 'approximately over 474 gigawatts' where the letter reads 'approximately 474 gigawatts'.
- 2026-08-19 · The directive has already moved a deadline. ERCOT stated on August 3rd that it would not tell service providers how any large load is classified in the Batch Zero study by the August 7th deadline. It said it would ask the utility commission for a good cause exception ahead of the August 20th open meeting. The Governor's office said on August 18th that the Data Center Coalition will comply. That release also says one data center that could not comply ended operations before construction began.
- 2026-08-20 · The exception ERCOT said it would seek is on the commission's agenda today. The published agenda for the August 20th open meeting lists Project 59142, the review of ERCOT's interconnection processes for large loads. The item includes discussion and possible action on an ERCOT request for a good cause exception. The same agenda lists Project 58481, the rulemaking to implement large load interconnection standards. Neither item is on the agenda's list of matters to be taken up without discussion.
- 2026-08-23 · The exception was granted. The commission signed an order in Project No. 59142 on August 20th. It lets the grid operator miss the August 7th classification deadline and pause the Batch Zero study of loads at 75 megawatts or more until the audit is done. The grid operator filed the audit's design the same day. It asks community impact information from data centers and crypto facilities of 25 megawatts or more that have not yet energized. That is a lower floor than the pause uses. It reports that 290 dynamic models have been reviewed, with approximately 18 percent acceptable on first review.
- 2026-08-25 · Checked and unchanged. Still pending, with no dated movement.
- 2026-08-26 · Checked and unchanged. The directive letter, the market notice and the commission's own filings still say what they said. The August 20th open meeting has come off the calendar feed now that it has been held, which is normal for that feed and not a change to the directive.
- 2026-08-27 · Checked and unchanged. The audit is still running and no data center has been cleared to advance. The August 20th open meeting that granted the exception has been held. The next public step on the calendar is the December 17th open meeting, the one the audit's own filed schedule ends on.
- 2026-08-28 · Checked and unchanged. The directive still requires the audit to finish before any data center project moves forward, and neither the commission nor ERCOT has published a result. Every project in the queue is still waiting on it.
- 2026-08-29 · Checked and unchanged. The directive still tells the utility commission and the grid operator to audit every data center in the interconnection process before any of them advances. No completed audit has been published, so what the audit found is still unknown.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The Governor directed the commission and ERCOT to audit all data centers in the interconnection process.

> Governor Greg Abbott today directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT's interconnection process.

Source (primary_official): https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-directs-comprehensive-data-center-audit

### The audit must be complete before any project advances, and a failing project is denied connection.

> The PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward. Any project that fails to comply with the requirements set forth by the PUCT and ERCOT will be denied connection to the Texas grid.

Source (primary_official): https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-directs-comprehensive-data-center-audit

### The directive letter states the size of the interconnection queue against the record peak.

> The Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) is currently considering approximately 474 gigawatts of requests to connect to the Texas grid. That is more than five times Texas' record peak electricity demand for ERCOT.

Source (primary_official): https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-directs-comprehensive-data-center-audit

Source (primary_official): https://ftp.puc.texas.gov/public/puct-info/agency/om/082026Final.pdf

Source (primary_official): https://ftp.puc.texas.gov/public/puct-info/agency/om/082026Final.pdf

### The commission granted the exceptions ERCOT asked for, and gave its reason.

### The order records that the grid operator is pausing the study of loads at or above the large load threshold.

> In response, ERCOT intends to temporarily pause its transitional Batch Zero interconnection study of loads that are 75 MW or more (Large Loads), including data centers and virtual currency mining facilities, until the verification and audit are complete.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_53_1675960.PDF

### The community impact half of the audit reaches a lower threshold than the pause does.

> As part of the same effort, ERCOT will request the community impact information identified in the Governor's letter from all data centers and virtual currency mining facilities of 25 MW or more that have not yet energized.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_53_1675960.PDF

### The order states how long the work is expected to take.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_53_1675960.PDF

### The grid operator reported how many technical models it had reviewed and how many passed on the first look.

> ERCOT has reviewed 290 dynamic models and approximately 18% were acceptable on first review

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### The filing defines the two size bands the audit uses.

> Large loads: 75 MW or greater | Medium loads: At least 25 MW and less than 75 MW

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### The community impact request goes to projects at or above the medium load floor that have not switched on.

> ERCOT will request information from data center and crypto facilities that have requested 25 MW or more and have yet to energize

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### The filing gives the size of the medium load population the community impact review will refresh.

> April snapshot had 157 medium data center and crypto loads totaling approximately 8,766 MW

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### Projects that had cleared every other step are the ones the energization pause holds.

> 17 large loads (6,608 MW total peak demand over 5 years) | These large loads have finished all ERCOT processes except have not received ERCOT's approval to energize.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### Both reports are due on the same December date and go to an open meeting a week later.

> December 10 | File Batch Zero Eligibility Verification Report | December 17 | Commission Open Meeting

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### A load that does not clear verification, or stays silent, is put out of the study.

> Large loads that do not pass verification, or do not respond, will be disqualified from Batch Zero

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

### The grid operator asked to classify loads conditionally by a new date rather than the one it missed.

> To excuse ERCOT from the August 7, 2026 classification deadline in Planning Guide § 9.3.1(2)(a) and instead allow ERCOT to conditionally classify large loads by August 31, 2026.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59142_52_1675837.ZIP

# Pflugerville orders a November election on charter amendments, one of them a section on the city's use of artificial intelligence

The Pflugerville City Council approved on second reading on August 11th, 2026 an ordinance ordering a special election on November 3rd, 2026 on amendments to the city's home rule charter. The 2026 Charter Review Commission put 21 amendments forward for the city's voters. One of them adds a new Section 2.03 titled Artificial Intelligence Protections. It would require the council to adopt protections covering data, facial recognition and surveillance technology. It would also require transparent approval processes for those technologies and a responsible artificial intelligence framework. A charter section outlives the council that writes it, which an ordinary policy does not.

- Topic: surveillance-and-policing
- Decided by: Pflugerville City Council (city)
- Where: Travis, Williamson
- Statistical areas:
  - Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX
- Status: open
- Public access: Comment window open
- Comment closes: 2026-11-03
- Take part: https://legistar1.granicus.com/Pflugerville/attachments/1d648f39-3bbb-4159-a4a7-a3c19b80bfcd.pdf

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2026-08-11 · ordered: Ordinance ordering the election approved on second reading
- 2026-11-03 · comment closes: Election day, the last day a voter can answer the question

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-20 · Admitted. The Charter Review Commission's filed report carries the full text of the proposed Section 2.03 and the ordinance setting the election date.
- 2026-08-20 · The election ordinance itself is now on the record beside the commission's report. It sets November 3rd, 2026 with polls open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. The commission put 21 amendments forward. The wording each proposition will carry on the ballot is in an exhibit to the ordinance and is unconfirmed, so what is published here is the section the commission recommends.
- 2026-08-23 · Checked and unchanged. The city's own legislative record shows the ordinance ordering the charter election approved on second reading on August 11th, with all members voting in favor. No later action is recorded on it. The election is still set for November 3rd.
- 2026-08-26 · The comment window is still open, closing November 3rd.
- 2026-08-29 · The comment window is still open, closing November 3rd. The charter amendment adding a section on the city's use of artificial intelligence is still one of those the voters decide, and the council has not withdrawn it.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The proposed charter section states what the council would be required to adopt.

> City Council shall adopt protections governing the collection, use, retention, and oversight of data, facial recognition, and surveillance technologies; establish transparent approval processes for such technologies; require a responsible AI (artificial intelligence) framework; ensuring this information is used locally for a legitimate basis established by law.

# PUCT Docket 59029, Oncor application for a second 765 kV line across ten west Texas counties

Oncor Electric Delivery has applied to amend its certificate of convenience and necessity to build the Longshore Switch to Drill Hole Switch transmission line. The application covers ten named counties in west Texas. The commission has it set for discussion and possible action at the open meeting on August 21st, 2026. That agenda carries this application and the Dinosaur Switch to Longshore Switch application and nothing else. The two lines meet at Longshore Switch. The commission issued its order on August 28th, 2026, amending the certificate to include the line and approving route 476. The two applications had been consolidated on the question of need and were severed again so each could take its own final order.

# House Public Health held an interim hearing on artificial intelligence use in health care

The Texas House Committee on Public Health met on August 20th, 2026 on a charge about clinical artificial intelligence. It directs the committee to study the use of artificial intelligence in the health care system to improve access and quality and efficiency of care. The same charge tells the committee to evaluate potential risks to patient safety and privacy and access to care for Texans. A second charge on the same agenda covers what social media platforms and artificial intelligence technologies do to the mental health and the cognitive development of minors. This is the committee that would write any statute governing clinical AI in the next session. Clinical AI is already running in Texas hospitals.

# NSF awarded Prairie View A and M a grant to let AI split up the grid optimization problem across processor cores

The National Science Foundation made an award to Prairie View A and M University on August 11th, 2026 under its HBCU Excellence in Research program. The project builds a framework that uses graph based artificial intelligence and reinforcement learning to decide how to break up electric grid optimization problems. It then assigns the pieces to processor cores as the work runs. The award record states the obligation as FY 2026 = $699,999.00 and runs the project from October 1st, 2026 through September 30th, 2029. The math it targets is the math that decides which generators run in a grid the size of the one carrying the state's new load.

# NSF awarded UT Austin a grant to replace hand written robot safety rules with a model trained on demonstrated safe behavior

The National Science Foundation made an award to the University of Texas at Austin on August 13th, 2026 under its Foundational Research in Robotics program. The project trains a model on expert demonstrations and uses it as a filter that pulls a robot's action back toward behavior that was demonstrated as safe. The award record states the obligation as FY 2026 = $360,000.00 and runs the project from October 1st, 2026 through September 30th, 2029. Its own abstract is the argument for it, because it says engineers today must define every dangerous situation by hand.

- Topic: research-and-science

- Statistical areas:
  - Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX

### The abstract states how robot safety is specified today.

# UTMB moved its Epic health record into Microsoft's cloud and named advanced technologies as the reason

The University of Texas Medical Branch migrated its electronic health record from servers it runs itself onto Microsoft's Azure platform, and announced the move on August 13th, 2026. The institution states the cutover took nineteen minutes and that the migration was first announced as part of a five year agreement with Microsoft in May 2025. Its own account names a stronger foundation for advanced technologies that support patient care, research, education and operations. Where a public hospital's patient records physically sit is the decision that has to be made before any clinical AI tool reaches a bedside.

# National Science Foundation funds UT San Antonio and Texas A&M to adapt large language models on machines that can't afford to run them

The National Science Foundation made two matched standard grants on August 14th, 2026. They fund a subspace optimization framework for resource efficient and private fine tuning of large language models. One went to the University of Texas at San Antonio and one to Texas A&M University, each obligating the same amount. The award record states the problem as reaching the performance of full parameter fine tuning where computing resources are limited and training data are sensitive or off limits to share. It names small organizations, universities and healthcare institutions among those the current requirements shut out. Both awards run from January 1st, 2027 to December 31st, 2029.

# National Science Foundation funds Rice to let AI propose numerical algorithms only where a proof checker certifies them

The National Science Foundation made a standard grant to William Marsh Rice University in Houston on August 17th, 2026. The award record describes reinforcement learning and large language models proposing randomized numerical linear algebra algorithms. The Lean proof assistant is required to certify correctness and cost before a candidate counts. The record states that the machine methods can explore designs efficiently but may produce opaque or inconsistent results without dependable guarantees. It also describes separating real algorithmic improvement from variation caused by the model itself. The award runs from September 15th, 2026 to August 31st, 2029.

# A generative AI platform at UTMB reached the UT System Regents only on its third amendment, at $9,850,000, and now covers all seven health institutions

The University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston contracted in December 2024 for a platform giving it a secure way to work with generative artificial intelligence models. The agenda book for the August 12th and 13th, 2026 meeting of the University of Texas System Board of Regents carries the third amendment. It is item 65 on the consent agenda. It states the first agreement was set at $825,000 and did not require Board approval. A first amendment raised the value to $4,250,000 and still sat inside the same delegated authority. The third amendment adds $5,600,000 and brings the total to $9,850,000. It extends the platform to all seven University of Texas System health related institutions and is funded under an initiative appropriated by the 89th Texas Legislature. The agenda book also states the agreement was competitively procured. No minutes for the meeting are published, so what the Board did with the item is not yet on the public record.

- Topic: health-and-education
- Decided by: The University of Texas System Board of Regents (state-agency)

# UT System Regents put the first billion dollars of the UT Dell Medical Center into the capital program

The Board of Regents approved adding the first phase of the UT Dell Medical Center in Austin to the capital improvement program. It acted at its August 12th, 2026 meeting. The agenda book the board took up asks it to amend the program at a total project cost of one billion dollars for that phase. It also asks the board to appropriate that money from revenue financing system bond proceeds. The phase itself is early work and site preparation with a building cost of zero. The board item describes a 27 acre academic medical campus built around a digitally enabled infrastructure, with digital technology, robotics and automation folded into operations. It names MD Anderson as the partner for cancer care. The board's own document never uses the words artificial intelligence. That framing comes from the university's own April release, which describes a center where technology, data and AI are embedded to support clinicians. The debt is repaid from pledged revenues rather than from an appropriation, so the bet is on clinical income.

- Topic: health-and-education
- Decided by: University of Texas System Board of Regents (state-agency)
- Where: Travis
- Statistical areas:
  - Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Closed
- Take part: https://www.utsystem.edu/sites/default/files/offices/board-of-regents/board-meetings/agenda-book-full/8-2026AB.pdf

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

The AI framing on this campus comes from the university's own release and is attributed to it here.

# Texas requires AI training for state and local government employees, and this is the first annual cycle

House Bill 3512 of the 89th Regular Session created artificial intelligence training programs for certain employees and officials of state agencies and local governments. Its author was Giovanni Capriglione and its sponsor was Cesar Blanco. It took effect on September 1st, 2025. The Legislature indexes it under artificial intelligence and under the Department of Information Resources, which is the agency that certifies which programs satisfy it. Which programs carry that certification is unconfirmed. So is the date by which an entity files its compliance certification.

# NSF funds a Rice laboratory where a model designs the experiment and a robot runs it, bookable from anywhere

The National Science Foundation award to William Marsh Rice University funds READINESS, a cloud accessible robotic laboratory for synthesizing electronic and quantum materials. AI plans the experiments and the equipment executes them. The University of Texas at Austin is a collaborating institution. Rice describes the point as access rather than speed, putting capability that existed in a handful of laboratories behind a login a researcher anywhere in the country can use. The university's own framing is unusually careful about the limit, saying responsible AI should complement a researcher's judgment rather than replace it.

- Topic: research-and-science
- Decided by: National Science Foundation (federal)
- Where: Harris, Travis
- Statistical areas:
  - Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX
  - Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands, TX
- Status: decided
- Public access: Closed
- Take part: https://api.nsf.gov/services/v1/awards/2607553.json

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2026-08-01 · effective: Award start date recorded by the National Science Foundation

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-26 · Admitted. The award record and the university's own account agree on what the platform is and who may use it.
- 2026-08-29 · Checked and unchanged. The award to Rice still funds a laboratory where a model proposes the next experiment and a robot runs it. The university still frames the machine as complementing a researcher's judgment rather than replacing it. The platform is still described as one researchers elsewhere will be able to reach.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The award record names the project.

> PCL-Test Bed: Revolutionizing AI-Driven Autonomous Experimentation for Next-Generation Semiconductor Synthesis (READINESS)

Houston Methodist rolled out a suite of AI imaging tools across the system, starting with a small group of users before widening it. # UT Southwestern says AI now does most of the grading on its medical students' clinical exam notes

UT Southwestern Medical Center built a process that reads and grades the post encounter notes students write after their objective structured clinical examinations. The medical school says it has replaced more than 91 percent of human grading since the autumn of 2023 and returns results in days rather than weeks. The stated reason is that grading those notes by hand is slow and inconsistent. The page names no model and no vendor, and it carries no publication date, so how current the figure is can't be established from it.

UT Arlington leads a project on keeping AI driven experiment workflows trustworthy at large scientific facilities. Texas A&M announced its own participation five days later. The program routes federal science money through an explicitly AI first frame, so Texas campuses are competing inside that frame rather than around it. # National Science Foundation funds a five year human and robot co-adaptation center at UT Austin

The National Science Foundation made award 2535195 to the University of Texas at Austin on August 25th, 2026. It funds a Science and Technology Center on human and robot co adaptation. The award record carries an estimated total for the full five years in the agency's own award service. It records the fiscal year 2026 obligation as $5,999,999.00. The project runs from September 1st, 2026 to August 31st, 2031. Joydeep Biswas is the principal investigator. The stated problem is that robots leaving the laboratory for homes and hospitals and workplaces have to understand and adapt to people over time. The university names the places the work runs in. They are houses and dorms and cafes and a public museum and a rehabilitation hospital and elder care and assisted living residences. It also states that an internal ethics board will oversee the research and develop the consent and opt out procedures. The rooms are named and the rules for the people in them are not written yet.

- Topic: research-and-science
- Decided by: United States National Science Foundation (federal)

- Statistical areas:
  - Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos, TX

# A statewide poll finds most Texas voters oppose a data center in their own community for a second survey running

The Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin polled 1200 registered Texas voters from August 5th to 13th, 2026. It reported that 57 percent oppose the construction of a data center in their community. Only 30 percent expressed support. The project calls the result statistically indistinguishable from its June reading. Republicans split closely in August at 45 percent supporting against 43 percent opposing. Democrats and independents stayed decisively opposed.

- Topic: data-centers
- Decided by: Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin (state-agency)
- Where: Statewide
- Status: decided
- Public access: Write to the decider
- Take part: https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/blog/new-ut-texas-politics-project-poll-finds-talarico-leading-paxton-abbott-leading-hinojosa-continued-resistance-to-data-centers-2

- Last checked: 2026-08-27

## Dates

- 2026-08-13 · filed: Last day of the polling field period

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-27 · Admitted. The project's own release carries the split, the field dates, the sample size and the margin of error.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The project reports the split on building a data center locally.

> For the second consecutive survey, a majority of Texans, 57%, said that they oppose the construction of a data center in their community, while only 30% expressed support, with the remaining 14% expressing no opinion.

Source (primary_official): https://texaspolitics.utexas.edu/blog/new-ut-texas-politics-project-poll-finds-talarico-leading-paxton-abbott-leading-hinojosa-continued-resistance-to-data-centers-2

### The project states its field period, its sample and its margin of error.

> The poll was conducted August 5-13, 2026, among 1200 registered voters in Texas. The margin of error for the survey is +/- 2.83% (3.58% when accounting for the weighted sample).

# PUCT opens the first five year review of the ERCOT system-wide offer caps, with comments due September 17th

The Public Utility Commission of Texas has opened Project 59550, the quinquennial review of the system-wide offer cap programs under 16 TAC Section 25.509(d). Commission staff filed a memorandum on August 20th, 2026 asking interested parties to answer questions about whether the caps and the emergency pricing program should change. The memorandum states that calendar year 2026 marks the first review period for these programs. It also states that ERCOT has never activated the emergency pricing program since it was adopted. Comments are due by September 17th, 2026 and anyone may file one through the commission's Interchange.

- Topic: power-and-the-grid
- Decided by: Public Utility Commission of Texas (state-agency)
- Where: Statewide
- Status: open
- Public access: Comment window open
- Comment closes: 2026-09-17
- Take part: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/search/filings/?UtilityType=A&ControlNumber=59550&ItemMatch=Equal&DocumentType=ALL&SortOrder=Ascending

- Last checked: 2026-08-28

- 2026-03-23 · filed: Market Analysis requests a new control number for the review
- 2026-08-20 · comment opens: Staff memorandum asking for comments filed as item 2

# PUCT told an Armstrong County AI data center to shed its whole load, and the data center asked for a rehearing

The Public Utility Commission of Texas approved a net metering arrangement in Docket 59220 on July 24th, 2026. It lets a second AI data center complex share the point of interconnection and the settlement meter of GOODNIT1, a stand-alone wind resource in Armstrong County. The commission attached conditions. The second load has to curtail fully when ERCOT instructs, and it may not be offered into any demand response program the order names. Neither complex is running yet and the commission found ownership of the second load has not transferred to the company expected to operate it. Ensign Infrastructure filed a motion for rehearing on August 18th, 2026 asking the commission to find that no conditions are necessary, and the commission has not ruled on it.

- Topic: data-centers
- Decided by: Public Utility Commission of Texas (state-agency)
- Where: Armstrong
- Statistical areas:
  - Amarillo, TX
- Status: pending
- Public access: Write to the decider
- Take part: https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/search/filings/?UtilityType=A&ControlNumber=59220&ItemMatch=Equal&DocumentType=ALL&SortOrder=Ascending

- Last checked: 2026-08-28

## Dates

- 2026-01-09 · filed: Joint application for net metering approval
- 2026-03-26 · filed: Amended application naming Ensign as the large load customer
- 2026-05-29 · filed: ERCOT files its study results and recommendations
- 2026-07-24 · ordered: Commission order approving the arrangement with conditions
- 2026-08-18 · filed: Ensign Infrastructure files a motion for rehearing

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-28 · Admitted on the commission's own order and the motion for rehearing, both read as filed documents. The arrangement is approved and the conditions stand while the rehearing motion is undecided.
- 2026-08-28 · What the commission ordered reaches the second load and names it. An earlier order on the first load carries its own curtailment condition and is a separate proceeding. The two are quoted separately here because the difference is the whole of what the rehearing motion disputes.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The docket's official case style names the three applicants and what they asked for.

> APPLICATION OF CRUSOE ENERGY SYSTEMS LLC, FGE GOODNIGHT I, LLC AND ENSIGN INFRASTRUCTURE LLC FOR APPROVAL OF A NET METERING ARRANGEMENT

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/search/filings/?UtilityType=A&ControlNumber=59220&ItemMatch=Equal&DocumentType=ALL&SortOrder=Ascending

### The commission approved the arrangement and attached conditions to it.

> The Commission approves the net metering arrangement, subject to the conditions imposed by this Order.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission's findings give the generator's capacity and the county it stands in.

> Goodnight owns and operates GOODNIT1, a stand-alone 265.5-MW wind generation resource in Armstrong County.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission found Ensign is the intended customer the applicants say will take over both loads once they are built.

> Ensign is the intended large load customer that the applicants state will take over and operate both the Crusoe One and Crusoe Two loads upon their completion and energization.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission's findings give both data center complexes their size and put both in Armstrong County.

> Crusoe is the current owner and developer of two AI data-center complexes located in Armstrong County: a 265-MW data center complex referred to as "the Crusoe One Load" and a 260-MW AI data-center complex referred to as "the Crusoe Two Load."

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission found both loads sit at the generator's own point of interconnection.

> the Crusoe One and Crusoe Two loads will be co-located with GOODNIT1 and interconnected at the GOODNIT1 point of interconnection

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission gave its reason for weighing both loads together rather than only the new one.

> it is appropriate to consider both loads when evaluating the net metering arrangement for the Crusoe Two load.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The order's first condition requires the second load to come off entirely when ERCOT instructs it.

> Crusoe and Ensign must ensure that the Crusoe Two Load fully curtails its consumption in the manner directed by ERCOT

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The order sets a 30 minute window and lets the operators cut it to 10 minutes by telling ERCOT in writing they can.

> Crusoe or Ensign may reduce the required time period from 30 minutes to 10 minutes by providing written confirmation to ERCOT of the Crusoe Two Load's capability to curtail within 10 minutes.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### ERCOT gives notice ahead of the instruction where it can, as a floor rather than a fixed period.

> When practicable, ERCOT must provide at least 60 minutes of notice in advance

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The order bars the second load from every demand response program it names.

> Crusoe and Ensign may not allow the Crusoe Two Load to be offered into or to participate in any ERCOT or transmission or distribution service provider (TDSP) demand response product, program, or service, including without limitation any Ancillary Service, ERCOT's Emergency Response Service, any ERCOT-procured contract for capacity, or any TDSP load management program.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The order records the figure Ensign and Crusoe argued the two conditions add up to. It is their contention and the commission does not adopt it.

> it would result in a total curtailment of 525.5 MW

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### Commission staff and ERCOT answered that a second wind resource which has not been built should be left out of the case.

> GOODNIT2 does not yet exist, is not a part of the application, and should not be considered in this proceeding.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission had imposed the same conditions once before, in the case the order calls the only other one to reach a final decision.

> the Commission also imposed identical conditions in Docket No. 58872

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The order refused every request it did not expressly grant.

> The Commission denies all other motions and any other requests for general or specific relief, if not expressly granted.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The commission found the second load has not changed hands and that Ensign may yet not be the customer.

> ownership and control of the Crusoe Two Load has not yet transferred to Ensign, making it less than certain that Ensign will replace Crusoe as the large load customer

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_69_1668205.PDF

### The company that will operate the load says the order goes beyond what the statute allows.

> exceeds what is required or authorized under PURA § 39.169

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion says the order left the central legal question unanswered.

> Nor did the Order directly address the critical legal and policy issue of first impression that underlies this case

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion states how it characterizes the order.

> the Order is excessive, arbitrary and capricious, unsupported by the evidentiary record, and not authorized by the language of PURA.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion argues the duty should be sized to the existing generator the statute is about.

> the curtailment obligation should be calibrated to the size of the existing generator that is subject to PURA

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion names the day it was served.

> was served on all parties of record in this proceeding on this 18th day of August, 2026

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion asks the commission to delete the conditions rather than shrink them.

> Ensign respectfully asks the Commission to grant rehearing and amend its Order to find that no conditions are necessary on Crusoe Two.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

### The motion names exactly what it is challenging.

> Ensign respectfully raises points of error to Findings of Fact 57 and 58, Conclusions of Law 9 and 10, and Ordering Paragraph 1.

Source (primary_official): https://interchange.puc.texas.gov/Documents/59220_73_1675222.PDF

# Senate Economic Development takes up AI and the Texas workforce in a September 3rd hearing

The Senate Committee on Economic Development carries an interim charge on preparing the Texas workforce for artificial intelligence. The charge directs the committee to study what AI does to the Texas workforce and what that means for the state's economic competitiveness. It also directs the committee to look at workforce resiliency. Educational pathways set against evolving employer needs and opportunities for upskilling are named in the same charge. The Legislature's own upcoming meetings listing sets the committee for Thursday, September 3rd, 2026 at 9:00 AM in hearing room E1.016 at the Capitol and marks it a public hearing. Angela Paxton chairs the committee and Kevin Sparks is vice chair.

- Topic: state-policy
- Decided by: Texas Senate Committee on Economic Development (legislature)
- Where: Statewide
- Status: open
- Public access: Public meeting
- Take part: https://capitol.texas.gov/Committees/MeetingsUpcoming.aspx?Chamber=S

- Last checked: 2026-08-29

## Dates

- 2026-09-03 · hearing: Public hearing, 9:00 AM, hearing room E1.016

## How this decision moved

One dated line per check, oldest first. A line that says nothing changed means somebody looked and it had not.

- 2026-08-29 · Admitted. The committee's own page carries the interim charge on preparing the Texas workforce for artificial intelligence. The Legislature's upcoming meetings listing sets the hearing for September 3rd in hearing room E1.016. The listing marks it a public hearing rather than a work session.

## Evidence

Every fact above rests on one of these. The words are the source's own.

### The committee's interim charge directs it to study what artificial intelligence does to the Texas workforce.

> Preparing the Texas Workforce for AI (Artificial Intelligence): Study the impact of AI on the Texas workforce and its implications for economic competitiveness.

Source (primary_official): https://senate.texas.gov/cmte.php?c=525

### The same charge names what else the committee is to evaluate.

> Evaluate strategies to enhance workforce resiliency, align educational pathways with evolving employer needs, and promote private-sector-led innovation.

Source (primary_official): https://senate.texas.gov/cmte.php?c=525

### The charge asks the committee to identify upskilling opportunities and to make recommendations.

> Identify opportunities for upskilling and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies to maximize employment opportunities.

Source (primary_official): https://senate.texas.gov/cmte.php?c=525

### The Legislature's own upcoming meetings listing carries the committee, the date, the time, the room and that it is a public hearing.

> Thursday, September 3, 2026 9:00 AM Economic Development Type: Public Hearing Location: E1.016 (Hearing Room)

Source (primary_official): https://capitol.texas.gov/Committees/MeetingsUpcoming.aspx?Chamber=S

### The committee's own page names who chairs it.

> CHAIR Angela Paxton VICE-CHAIR Kevin Sparks

Source (primary_official): https://senate.texas.gov/cmte.php?c=525
